metadata.title: ONCA Procedural Decision Breakdown (2020-2026)
metadata.description: Ontario Court of Appeal decision types - showing procedural vs. substantive outcomes
metadata.data_quality: Procedurally classified from decision text; worker injury cases represent minority (~1%)
metadata.key_insight: ONCA decisions are predominantly procedural (dismissals, costs awards, motions). Use for precedent research, not outcome comparison.

dismissed.label: Dismissed
dismissed.description: Application/appeal denied on procedural or jurisdictional grounds

costs_awarded.label: Costs Awarded
costs_awarded.description: Party ordered to pay other side's legal costs
examples: Appellant ordered to pay $50K respondent costs

motion_decided.label: Motion Decided
examples: Stay of lower court decision pending appeal

remitted.label: Remitted/Sent Back
remitted.description: Case sent back to lower tribunal/court for reconsideration
examples: Appeal allowed in part; remitted for new hearing

allowed_substantive.label: Appeal Allowed (Substantive)
examples: Appeal allowed; lower court decision reversed

reserved.label: Decision Reserved
reserved.description: Judgment pending (appeal heard but not yet decided)
examples: Decision reserved (pending from prior hearing year)

worker_injury_cases.note: ONCA decisions include appeals from all tribunal types. Worker injury cases represent ~1% of scrape results.
examples: WSIAT decision appealed to ONCA on legal interpretation
HRTO decision appealed for procedural fairness violation
ONSBT decision appealed on jurisdictional grounds
worker_injury_cases.key_finding: Most worker injury appeals that reach ONCA are on narrow procedural grounds (Leave was wrongly denied, tribunal lacked jurisdiction). Substantive merit reversals are rare.

success_rates.substantive_success_definition: Appeal allowed in full or in part
success_rates.interpretation: ONCA's role is appellate review for legal error. Most applications denied at leave stage. Substantive success rate reflects very narrow scope.

use_cases.precedent_research: ✅ Primary use—search ONCA decisions for legal interpretation relevant to your case
use_cases.outcome_comparison: ❌ NOT recommended—ONCA is appellate, not first-level tribunal. Outcomes are procedural, not merit-based.
use_cases.appeal_strategy: ✅ Use to understand leave to appeal standards and what grounds succeed
use_cases.legal_interpretation: ✅ Use to see how courts interpret tribunal statutes and standards of review

methodology.data_source: Ontario Court of Appeal decisions via CanLII (2020-2026)
methodology.classification_method: Regex pattern matching on decision headers and disposition text
methodology.confidence: 93.7% (procedural classification is explicit in ONCA decisions)
methodology.limitations: Worker injury cases represent ~1% of total; sample size for substantive appeals is small. Temporal data reflects publication timing, not decision date.
